chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: All three energy into damage plus the free attack. All Streams Flow to the Sea first, into Seapunk: printed 9 plus Charge 8 read at one point per two Charge is 4, so 13. I led with it in case the scaling resource is spent or drifts once other cards resolve. Then both Water's Edge for 6 each, then Gorou — Inuzaka All-Round Defense, which is 0 cost, for 6 more and exhausts itself. Total 31 into a 40 HP enemy, leaving it at 9. I eat the 11 and go to 37/70. The point of the line is that 9 HP is trivially inside next turn's reach — the third Water's Edge alone nearly covers it, and any two of my remaining attacks bury it — so this turn buys a guaranteed kill next turn while paying exactly one hit for it.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: The block line: both Coral Guard for 10 Block plus one Water's Edge, or Thoma - Blazing Ooyoroi on its Block mode. Ten Block against an 11 telegraph reduces the hit to 1, which is nearly free mitigation and reads well in isolation. I rejected it because it does not change how many hits I take, it increases them. Nothing on this board kills the enemy this turn — 40 HP is out of reach even with everything — so the question is how many enemy turns the fight lasts. Racing at 31 makes the fight two turns and one incoming hit. Blocking for 10 and dealing ~6 makes it at least three turns and two more incoming hits after this one, and the second hit costs more than the 10 Block saved. I also weighed Tactical Retreat as a free cantrip, but discard 1 random with a hand this loaded can eat All Streams Flow to the Sea or a Water's Edge, and I had no energy left for whatever it drew anyway.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: All the defense. I take the full 11 with 0 Block, dropping to 37/70, when 10 of that was cheaply preventable. It also spends Gorou permanently — Exhaust means that 6 damage is gone from the deck for the rest of the fight — to shave a turn I would probably have won anyway; if next turn's draw is dead, burning Gorou now is a real loss. And it leaves Thoma, both Coral Guard, and the third Water's Edge unplayed, so if the enemy's next telegraph is a large hit I face it with whatever the draw hands me rather than a stocked hand.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. The 11 is small enough to eat and the enemy is far enough out of kill range that racing wins. Two changes would flip it. If the telegraph were a heavy hit — call it 20 or more — the arithmetic of trading HP for tempo stops working and I would spend both Coral Guard and Thoma's Block mode, keeping Gorou unexhausted. And if the enemy were showing a defensive or buffing intent rather than an attack, I would drop Gorou from the line entirely: with no incoming damage there is no clock to beat, so I would deal 25 with the three energy and keep the exhaust card banked. A telegraphed block on the enemy's side would also make me reconsider dumping everything into a wall.
